issues.description: The problem text (Part 2) specifies messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) with a double parameter and a return string including the milk volume, but the UML earlier in the problem, the template usage in Main.java, and the solution implementation define Milkable.messageOnMilk() with no parameters. This contradiction leaves students unclear whether the milk-volume parameter should be part of the interface and how to call the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the mismatch by choosing one consistent signature: either (A) keep Milkable.messageOnMilk() parameterless and update the problem text to remove mention of a milkVolume parameter and volume formatting, or (B) change the interface to messageOnMilk(double milkVolume), update all implementations (Seal, Goat) and the template Main to call messageOnMilk(...) with a double argument, and update the UML accordingly. Document the chosen API in the problem statement and UML so students can implement without ambiguity.

issues.description: The problem statement text requires a method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (including a double parameter and volume in the return string), but the UML, template usage, and solution code define and use messageOnMilk() with no parameter. This mismatch in the method signature (and expected output format) creates confusion about the exact method students must implement and will lead to compilation or test failures if students follow the textual description rather than the provided code/UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the requirement consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement to require messageOnMilk() without parameters and remove the volume from the example return string, matching the UML/template/solution; or (B) change the interfaces and all implementations/usages to messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update all calls (e.g., Main and Farm) and the solution implementations to accept a double and include the volume in the returned string. Ensure tests, UML, template comments, and sample outputs are updated to the chosen signature.
